newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazilians confident about investing in stocks.
newsitem.headline: Brazilians confident about investing in stocks.

text.p: Middle to upper income Brazilians view investments in the stock market far more favorably than their counterparts in other countries, according to a survey by Brazil's National Development Bank (BNDES).

Whereas 69 percent of Brazilians surveyed agreed that people who invest in stocks make more profit than those who save, only 48 percent of Germans, 29 percent of British and nine percent of Italians think the same, the survey showed.

Fifty-seven percent of Brazilians believe that on the whole investing in stocks is profitable, and only 50 percent think buying stocks is a gamble, compared with 93 percent in Sweden, 84 percent in France, 77 percent in Britain and 62 percent in Italy.

Of those surveyed, 22 percent said they frequently thought of buying stocks, compared with 35 percent in Sweden and Ireland, 25 percent in Britain, 21 percent in Germany and 17 percent in Greece and Portugal.
The poll of 2,000 Brazilians aged 25 to 55, carried out by market researchers Ibope on behalf of the BNDES, comes only a few months ahead of one of Brazil's largest public share offers ever.

Under Brazil's privatization program, the government will be offering at the end of this year $1.8 billion worth in shares of mining giant CVRD and $1.2 billion worth of shares in power utility Light.
The shares remain to be sold after controlling stakes in each of the two companies were auctioned off to company investors earlier this year and last year.
The poll found that 65 percent of those interviewed approved of privatization, but only 46 percent had some knowledge about the process and the companies involved.
And only very few Brazilians are well informed about buying and selling shares, nine percent, whereas 39 percent have only some knowledge and 52 percent have no information whatsoever.
((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151))
